_readme: Club identity and static text. Edit this file (or point fetchers at a published Google Sheet) — no code changes needed.
_demo: true puts a banner above every tab saying the schedule, results and status on screen are invented. It is false because none of them are: those files are empty, waiting for real content, and the app says so in plain words where each one would go. Only set it true alongside stand-in content, and clear it in the same edit that removes it.
_tagline: One line under the club name, shown on every tab. Who the club is for, or when it plays. The header leaves the line out while this is empty.
_features: Which parts of the app are live. Turn each of these on when that phase's content is real — not when its code is written. A status panel nobody updates and an example yardage both teach players to distrust the app. 'status' is off until a named person has committed to updating data/status.json daily. 'yardage' and 'results' also take "preview": the tab appears and describes the feature, with no data behind it, which is what 'results' is on while there are no matches to show.
_scorecard: The scorecard needs no content, so it can be on from day one. 'holes' sets the card length when the course has not been mapped; once data/course.json has 'mapped': true the card follows the real hole count and shows par.
_sources: Optional published-CSV overrides. Set 'statusCsv' to a Google Sheet published to the web as CSV and the daily status comes from there instead of data/status.json, which stays as the fallback if the sheet is unreachable. Leave it empty to use the file. See 'The status sheet' in the README for the sheet layout.

homeCourse.name: Blair Academy Golf Course
homeCourse.note: The club's own course: the centre of the nine mapped holes in data/course.json, so the weather card and the Yardage tab are describing the same patch of ground. Change these only if the course does.
homeCourse._forecastUrl: Where the weather card's 'Full forecast and radar' link points. This is the National Weather Service page for the course, which is the right one for a US course. Leave it empty to build a Windy link from the coordinates above instead, which works anywhere.

_about: The club introduction, one string per paragraph. Who the club is for, what a typical week looks like, what a new member should expect at their first practice, whether beginners are welcome, whether clubs are provided, what it costs. Until someone writes it the About tab says the introduction has not been written yet, which is honest; placeholder prose pretending to be it is not.
_contacts: Role, name and an address each person is happy to have published. A name left empty reads 'TBD' rather than blank. Publishing a student's name here is the club's privacy decision, not this app's: a role with no name is a working answer.
_photos: Add image files to the repo and list them here as { "src", "caption" }. The Photos card hides itself while this is empty, so it never shows an empty grid.
